A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ComPO, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The retained material can be matched reliably despite additions, renumbering, and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM alignment experiments, benchmark scores, likelihood measurements, computational measurements, repeated-run results, and qualitative examples in Section 4 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds perturbation, clipping, layer, training-size, and DPO-initialization experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 adds a multi-layer adaptation that perturbs the MLPs in layers 30–31 alongside the output layer, extending v1's output-only practical implementation. The comparison oracle, gradient estimator, clipping and update rules, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use UltraFeedback for preference alignment and evaluate on AlpacaEval 2, Arena-Hard, and MT-Bench. The added studies remain within this coverage; no distinct data population, domain, or task is documented.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparators DPO, DPOclean, and SimPO remain. However, Section 4.3 and Appendix D newly include DPO and SimPO in the memory comparison, reporting 77 GB and 69 GB on H100 GPUs against approximately 23 GB for ComPO on A40 GPUs. v1's resource analysis reported ComPO measurements alone.

E3.justification: New experiments vary perturbations from 800 to 5400, one versus three perturbed layers, gradient thresholds, and 100 versus 300 noisy pairs. Table 10 compares ordinary-DPO and DPOclean initialization. The added Arena-Hard comparisons use GPT-4.1 judging rather than the original GPT-4 Turbo protocol. Existing benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled performance analyses of perturbation count, layer coverage, gradient clipping, and noisy-pair count in Tables 4–7, plus the initialization comparison in Table 10. These substantially expand validation of the practical heuristics beyond v1's sparsity plot, oracle-feedback robustness analysis, and qualitative examples, which are retained.

E5.justification: v1 already reports five-run means and standard deviations, best-of-five results, three likelihood trials, and eight-run oracle-feedback statistics. v2 retains these practices and applies the existing mean/standard-deviation reporting to added experiments. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure or increase in the original run counts is documented.

E6.justification: The original main and appendix table results are retained, while Tables 4–7 and 10 add substantial results. For example, Table 6 reports AlpacaEval LC of 23.42 ± 1.03 without clipping versus 25.91 ± 0.95 at lambda_g = 0.00022. Resource measurements are also added. New Arena-Hard scores use a different judge and are not same-setting revisions of earlier scores.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 drops the explicit beta > 0 condition from the background DPO loss description. This is a limited omission of a stated mathematical condition; the comparison-oracle definitions, Theorem 3.1, and Appendix C's propositions, lemmas, and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction's first contribution narrows its stated target from both verbosity and likelihood displacement to likelihood displacement. v2 explicitly says ComPO was not specifically designed to address verbosity, while retaining the empirical claim of benefits for both issues. The principal algorithmic and convergence contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of the perturbation and clipping tradeoffs, discusses difficulties in replacing the hard data threshold with confidence-based interpolation, and develops the applicability argument for refining existing aligned checkpoints. The limitations concerning offline learning, helpfulness-focused evaluation, and full-model perturbation are substantially retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access pointer alongside the existing model-release information. Appendix D newly reports approximately four hours of additional ComPO training and 12 minutes for pair division, plus hardware information for the memory comparison. Existing dataset links, checkpoint sources, and default settings remain.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds a focused discussion of learning from noisy preferences and compatibility with conditional DPO. Four references are added, covering preference variance, margin matching, Cal-DPO, and reward-augmented data. The established positioning relative to DPO and comparison-based optimization remains.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized revisions to the abstract, introduction, and limitations, adds Section 4.2, and expands and renames the efficiency subsection. Author and publication-header text also change. Most of the existing exposition and overall organization are retained.

P2.justification: Four new main-text tables and Appendix Table 10 substantially expand the result displays. Existing tables are resized or repositioned, Table 3 moves upward, and Figure 2 is reduced and regrouped with appendix statistics. The two figures' plotted content and the three qualitative examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important validation gap in the practical method: Tables 4–7 directly test clipping, perturbation budgets, layer restriction, and training-data scaling, while Table 10 tests whether clean-only DPO initialization is necessary. These controls substantially strengthen the evidence behind the practical design choices. Code-access and runtime information also improve reproducibility. The gains remain bounded by predominantly Mistral-based additions and by changed judges or hardware in some comparisons.
